text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwe's chief of intelligence Elleck Mashingaidze has been blinded by disease but President Robert Mugabe has allowed him to run the national secret service for a whole year, despite this handicap, authoritative sources said.
- Zimbabwe's annual inflation fell to 13.9 percent in November, the lowest level since 1989.

- A consortium of five black-owned Zimbabwean telecommunications companies has formed a Z$200 million joint venture with an unnamed South African firm to tender to operate Zimbabwe's second cellular network after one recently established by the state Posts and Telecommunications (PTC).

The project promoter Jacob Chamboko said the Zimbabwean partners in Zimcell had a 60 percent stake in the company, while the South African firm, held 40 percent and could be bought out at "an agreed time". The PTC has in the past year been locked in a legal battle to let another private cellular phone firm, Econet, set its own network but has been insisting that it goes through a tender system which many industry officials charge was specifically designed to keep Econet out.
- Zimbabwe's sixth commercial bank being set up by a consortium of local professional bankers and some institutional investors is expected to be launched in Harare in early 1997.

- The Zimbabwean government will invest money raised from its privatisation programme in new black-owned businesses as part of its efforts to economically empower the southern African country's majority black population, President Robert Mugabe told the official Herald newspaper. The government says it will initially warehouse proceeds from the privatisation programme in a National Investment Trust.

- The Zimbabwe government is working on regulations to guide child labour as currently there is a legal impediment to the practice, deputy agriculture minister Olivia Muchena said when she launched UNICEF's State of the World Children Report on Wednesday.
